messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Admission Date: November 2013
Discharge Date: January 2017
Length of Stay: 3 years and 2 months
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The 52-year-old male patient was diagnosed with a left temporal GBM in November 2013 after he presented with memory deficits and aphasia. He underwent standard radiation and temozolomide treatment initially. At the time of ketogenic diet therapy, the patient was on fifth-line treatment for recurrent GBM, which included the FDA-approved antiangiogenic therapy bevacizumab and irinotecan. Due to nausea, headaches, and fatigue, the patient started a ketogenic diet for 3.5 months. During the diet period, the patient was able to add physical exercise to his routine along with dance lessons. After discontinuation of the diet, the patient reported worsening symptoms, including difficulty reading and decreased short term memory. The patient's symptoms continued to progress, and he passed away in January 2017.

Clinical Findings:
During the hospital course, the patient reported memory deficits and aphasia. The initial treatment included standard radiation and temozolomide, followed by the antiangiogenic therapy bevacizumab and irinotecan. The patient was then switched to a ketogenic diet for 3.5 months, which resulted in increased physical activity, but also cravings for carbs and sweets. The patient's symptoms worsened after discontinuation of the diet, and his disease continued to progress until his death in January 2017.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient passed away due to the progression of his left temporal GBM.

Follow-Up:
The patient passed away in January 2017, and no further follow-up was possible.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Recurrent left temporal glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), a malignant neoplasm of the brain, drove this episode of care. Its treatment and progression continued until his death. Malignant neoplasms belong to chapter C, and brain malignancy is category C71.

CODE: C71
